about: The models the runner knows. Add one entry to add a model: `bench.py direct <name>` / `bench.py inside <name>` then use it, and `bench.py score` picks up its raw files (b_<name>_<set>.jsonl.gz directly, c_<name>_<set>.jsonl.gz inside solvi) and prints it under `label`. api: "chat" (default, an OpenAI-compatible chat-completions endpoint) or "systemone" (a decision model over the System One API; inside solvi it is a solvi.systemone decider). base_url and key_env are optional (default: OpenRouter's chat API, $OPENROUTER_API_KEY); extra is merged into every request (for a decision model on OpenRouter, the provider pin); direct_path: the path of a systemone model's direct requests (default /v1/systemone); price_in / price_out ($ per 1M tokens) are only a fallback for an endpoint that does not report usage.cost; latency (optional): the latency to show instead of the raw files' (per_decision, per_question, note), for a self-hosted model whose recorded times include queueing.

jev-1.13.label: Jev 1.13
jev-1.13.direct_path_note: the published run sent the direct requests to OpenRouter's Decisions API, which takes the same request as the System One API (/v1/systemone, used inside solvi)

jeeves.label: Jeeves (thinking)
jeeves.note: self-hosted: PostHog's Jeeves (github.com/PostHog/jeeves at f04ec55, weights PostHog/jeeves) served by its own `python -m inference.serve` on one A100 40 GB in bf16 (no FP8 on this GPU); no key, no per-request price; options = the authors' recommended fast setting

latency.note: Jeeves' own server on one A100 40 GB in bf16, one request at a time (median of 96 probe requests); the latencies in the raw files include queueing under concurrent requests
